summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic systolic heart failure, diabetes, and a history of coronary artery disease presented with fever, chills, weakness, and one day of upper back, left lower quadrant abdominal, and chest pain following dialysis. Initial concern for infection led to administration of vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam in the emergency department. Imaging showed small bilateral pleural effusions and mild pulmonary edema but no pneumonia or acute abdominal process. An ischemic-appearing right second toe prompted podiatry consultation, which found no active infection or need for surgical intervention. A minor debridement was performed to remove a callus. After ruling out bacterial sources, his symptoms were attributed to a nonspecific viral illness. He improved clinically, with resolution of fever and pain, and was discharged home on his baseline medications with instructions to resume dialysis and monitor for weight gain or toe complications.
problems: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the extremities, unspecified
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
